claim: Consider a binary incidence matrix with exactly five labeled habitats and \(s\ge2\) distinct species, each occurring in exactly two habitats. For species rows \(i<j\), define the classical checkerboard-unit count \(U_{ij}=(2-o_{ij})^2\), where \(o_{ij}\) is the number of habitats jointly occupied, and let \(U=\sum_{i<j}U_{ij}\) and \(C=U/\binom{s}{2}\). Then \(U\le 12s^2/11\), equivalently \(C\le24s/[11(s-1)]\). Equality is possible if and only if \(11\mid s\). When \(s=11t\), every equality matrix is, up to relabeling species and habitats, exactly the incidence pattern with \(5t\) species in habitats \(\{1,2\}\), \(2t\) species in each of \(\{3,4\},\{3,5\},\{4,5\}\), and no other habitat pairs. There are precisely ten distinct maximizing occupancy multiplicity vectors on five fixed labeled habitats. The four-habitat analogue has optimum \(U\le s^2\) attained by a balanced pair of disjoint habitat pairs whenever \(s\) is even, so five habitats first admit a strictly larger scale-free segregation ceiling, through an optimizer that itself contains intersecting habitat-pair types. The bound is for the unnormalized classical pairwise checkerboard score with no column-total constraint, not for a fixed-fixed null model or a software-specific normalized variant.
integrity: Universal optimization is reduced to a ten-variable rational quadratic simplex problem. Every face is checked by exact determinant signs and rational stationarity equations; the degenerate-face reduction and strict exterior-gradient argument establish exhaustive equality classification. Source temporal anchor 2013-01-09 is the earliest first-public exact day verified; the original 1990 paper has month-level publication evidence only.
scientific_limitations: Five habitats, all species occupying exactly two, classical unnormalized Stone–Roberts C-score; site richnesses are not fixed. The real bound is strict unless the number of species is divisible by eleven. No inference of ecological competition or null-model significance is claimed.
title: A sharp five-habitat checkerboard-score bound for species occupying exactly two sites
